facts.material: rubber cap with an embedded neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnet
facts.function: holds keys by magnetically attaching to metal surfaces

gri_path: GRI 1: the components are prima facie classifiable in different headings: the rubber cap in 4016 and the magnet in 8505 (permanent magnets and articles of permanent magnet)
GRI 3(b): the NdFeB magnet provides the article's function of attaching and holding keys, so it gives the essential character (GRI 3(c) would reach the same heading, 8505, as last in numerical order)
GRI 6: 8505.1 permanent magnets > 8505.11 of metal > 8505.11.00.70 sintered neodymium-iron-boron (assumed sintered)

rejected_alternatives.reason: the rubber cap is a housing; it does not give the essential character
permanent magnets other than of metal (e.g., ferrite/bonded in plastic); NdFeB is a metal magnet
applies only if the NdFeB magnet is bonded rather than sintered

missing_facts: Is the neodymium-iron-boron magnet sintered or bonded?
classification.rationale: The key cap is a composite good of a rubber cap and a neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnet. The magnet performs the article's function of attaching to metal surfaces to store keys, so under GRI 3(b) it controls, placing the article in 8505.11 as a metal permanent magnet and in statistical line .70 for sintered NdFeB. N333219 classified plastic articles backed with neodymium magnets in 8505.11.0070.
